title: Pork chops with swede, savoy and mustard

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a basic staple; chicken stock, wholegrain mustard and crème fraîche are all acceptable.

supermarket.reason: Pork chops, swede, savoy, apples and crème fraîche are everyday Tesco items at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: Needs only a wide lidded casserole and basic browning and simmering.

works.reason: Quantities suit four, 400ml stock suits a covered simmer, the swede cubes get 30 minutes, and the chops get about 15 minutes more after browning, which is enough; the apples will soften but hold up acceptably.

honest_times.reason: Peeling and cubing the swede, slicing, browning and softening fit roughly in 20 minutes, and the 30 cook minutes match the 15 + 10 + 5 in the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the sage, is used, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm braise of swede, savoy and apple suits early December, and the swede is the main vegetable, not a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: Brief, clear British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: A proper family dinner of pork with plenty of vegetables and a creamy mustard sauce.
